intro.title: Multiple State Variables
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user profile card component that displays and updates multiple independent pieces of information, such as a name, age, and online status. You will learn how to manage multiple state variables in a React component using the useState hook, each tracking its own value. The main technologies involved are React, TypeScript, and the useState hook for state management. This will teach you how to declare, update, and use several state variables separately within a single component. By the end, you'll understand how to handle distinct data points that can change independently over time.
intro.usecase: Managing multiple state variables is essential in real-world React applications where UI components need to track several independent pieces of data simultaneously. For example, in an e-commerce product page, you might need separate state variables for tracking quantity selection, color choice, size option, and whether the item has been added to the cart. Similarly, in a dashboard with multiple interactive filters, each filter (date range, category, status) would maintain its own state variable. This pattern allows developers to update specific UI aspects independently without affecting unrelated components, creating more responsive and maintainable user interfaces.
